solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Band’s sound causes fury (6)

indicatorNotes.sound: the letters come from how the word is said, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a collar is a band worn round the neck

annotation.surface: A rock group's noise is making somebody furious.
annotation.walkthrough: "Band" suggests musicians, which suits "sound"; it is a strip of cloth round the neck.
annotation.definitionFit: Choler is an old word for anger, from the bile once thought to cause it.

entries.clue: Close decision (10)

blocks.note: the close of a meeting is its end
the judgement reached after thinking it over

annotation.surface: A narrow verdict, as in a tight vote.
annotation.walkthrough: "Close decision" reads as one phrase, a tight call; "Close" is the noun meaning end, not the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A conclusion is both the end of something and the judgement arrived at.

entries.clue: Man missing from plots in French opera (7)

annotation.definitionNote: opera here is the Latin plural of opus, so it means works

indicatorNotes.missing from: the first word is absent from what follows, so take it out

blocks.note: manoeuvres are schemes or plots
the word itself, taken off the front

annotation.surface: A man has vanished from the storylines of an opera set in France.
annotation.walkthrough: "Opera" is not the sung drama but the plural of opus, works; the French word for works is oeuvres.
annotation.definitionFit: Oeuvres is French for works, and opera is Latin for the same thing, the plural of opus.

entries.clue: We finally came back prepared (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: at the end of the word, so its last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of "we"
came back with a witty reply, retorted

annotation.surface: Someone reports that the group returned at last, ready for anything.
annotation.walkthrough: "Came back" suggests returning home; it means answered back with a quip.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone kitted out with what the job needs is ready for it.

entries.clue: Bid to catch complete miscreant (8)

indicatorNotes.to catch: the first word holds the next one inside it

blocks.note: a bid is an offer
to complete is to end

annotation.surface: An attempt to arrest a thorough villain.
annotation.walkthrough: "Complete" looks like an adjective describing the miscreant; it is the verb, to end.
annotation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who has broken the law, a miscreant.

entries.clue: She who isn’t really a good speller? (5,9)

annotation.definition: She who isn’t really a good speller?

blocks.note: a figure from fairy tales, not a real person
not someone who spells words well but someone who casts kind spells

annotation.surface: A woman who is not actually much good at spelling.
annotation.walkthrough: "Good speller" suggests spelling tests; the question mark flags the other spell, magic, and a kind witch.
annotation.definitionFit: Cinderella's fairy godmother casts benevolent spells, and she exists only in stories.

entries.clue: Young flier, say, without a permit (6)

indicatorNotes.without: in its old sense of outside, so the first piece wraps round the next

blocks.note: e.g. = for example, which is what "say" means here
the letter itself, held inside EG
to let is to permit

annotation.surface: A young pilot flying without a licence.
annotation.walkthrough: "Without" reads as lacking; here it means outside, so EG goes round A.
annotation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a bird still learning to fly.

entries.clue: PIN number? (4,3)

blocks.note: not a bank code but a pin, slang for a leg
not a figure but something that numbs, read as num-ber

annotation.surface: A request for the code for a bank card.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pins" is slang for legs, and "number" is something that makes you numb. A dead leg is the numbing blow to the thigh schoolchildren give each other.
annotation.definitionFit: A dead leg is a leg left numb, often by a knee to the thigh, so a pin made number.

entries.clue: Busy bee’s missed chance (4)

indicatorNotes.missed: the bee is left out of the word

blocks.note: busy, lively
bee is how the letter B is spelt out, and that letter is the one dropped

annotation.surface: A busy bee has let an opportunity slip.
annotation.walkthrough: "Busy bee" reads as one hard worker; "bee" is the letter B.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: a chance of things going wrong, as in "a risk of rain".

entries.clue: Cutting off inner cities had to be silly (14)

indicatorNotes.silly: the letters are to be jumbled into nonsense

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Cutting services to deprived urban areas was a foolish policy.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cutting off" suggests funding or supplies; it is cutting someone out of a will.
annotation.definitionFit: To cut someone off, without a penny, is to disinherit them; disinheritance is the act.

entries.clue: Island’s gold seized by returning vessel (5)

indicatorNotes.seized by: gold is held inside the vessel
indicatorNotes.returning: the vessel runs back the other way

blocks.note: an urn is a vessel, a vase or jar
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: An island's gold is captured by a ship sailing home.
annotation.walkthrough: "Vessel" wants to be a ship; it is a pot. Nauru is a small island nation in the Pacific.
annotation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny island republic in Micronesia, once rich from phosphate mining.

entries.clue: Jelly can now be drunk? (9)

blocks.note: a gelatin made from fish bladders
split the answer into three short words and they describe a drink already poured and ready

annotation.surface: A question whether a jelly has turned liquid enough to drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: split ISINGLASS as IS IN GLASS and it describes a poured drink, which can now be drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a pure gelatin from fish, used to clear beer and wine, so a jelly.

entries.clue: God can shut up minister (4,5,4)

blocks.note: the Lord is God
can is slang for a toilet, and so is privy
to seal something is to shut it up

annotation.surface: A deity is able to silence a clergyman.
annotation.walkthrough: "Can" looks like the verb, and "minister" like a priest; can is a toilet and the minister is in the British cabinet.
annotation.definitionFit: The Lord Privy Seal is a senior British government minister, a post that now carries no department.

entries.clue: On surveying house, one may see problems (10)

annotation.definition: On surveying house, one may see problems

blocks.note: not a building survey but a look at one of the twelve houses of the zodiac
not structural faults but troubles foretold in the stars

annotation.surface: A surveyor inspecting a property finds defects.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a house survey; in astrology the sky is split into twelve houses, and reading them predicts trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: An astrologer reads the planets' positions in the houses of a birth chart and forecasts trouble ahead.

entries.clue: Group of women with similar habits (10)

annotation.definition: Group of women with similar habits

blocks.note: a body of women, such as a religious order
not routines but the robes nuns wear

annotation.surface: Some women who share the same routines.
annotation.walkthrough: "Habits" suggests behaviour; it is the nun's garment.
annotation.definitionFit: A sisterhood is a community of nuns, who all wear the same habit.

entries.clue: No cap on pay for a long time (4)

indicatorNotes.No cap on: a cap sits on top, so take off the first letter

blocks.note: wages are pay
the top letter, removed

annotation.surface: Salaries have gone uncapped for years.
annotation.walkthrough: "No cap on pay" reads as an unlimited salary; it asks for WAGES without its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Ages means a very long time, as in "I waited for ages".

entries.clue: Retreat in fear, swinging light (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the first piece goes inside the second
indicatorNotes.swinging: the letters of fear swing into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of fear, rearranged
a nest is a snug retreat

annotation.surface: Someone backs away in terror from a swaying lamp.
annotation.walkthrough: "Light" looks like a lamp to go with "swinging"; it is a window. Fenestra is Latin for window and survives in anatomy and architecture.
annotation.definitionFit: A light is a window or pane, and fenestra is the Latin word for a window opening.

entries.clue: Order parts for old wind instrument (4)

indicatorNotes.parts for: the order splits open to let the next piece in

blocks.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, a British honour
o = old, a standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Someone orders spare parts for an antique woodwind.
annotation.walkthrough: "Order parts" reads as buying spares; the Order parts to let O inside.
annotation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind, so a wind instrument.

entries.clue: Fabric made from skin, eg — skin of zebra? (7)

indicatorNotes.skin of: the skin is the outside, so the first and last letters

blocks.note: the skin is an example of an organ, the body's largest
the outside letters of zebra

annotation.surface: A textile made from animal hide, such as a zebra's pelt.
annotation.walkthrough: "Skin" appears twice doing two jobs: first as an example of an organ, then as the outer letters of zebra.
annotation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff sheer fabric, often silk, used for evening wear.

entries.clue: Who delivers curtains for you? (4,6)

blocks.note: not a soft-furnishings supplier; curtains is slang for the end, death
the question mark flags that curtains is not drapes

annotation.surface: Asking which shop will bring your new curtains to the house.
annotation.walkthrough: "It's curtains for you" means you are finished; the figure who brings death is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Grim Reaper is death personified, the robed figure with a scythe who comes for you.

entries.clue: Performer, thespian is terrible in part (7)

indicatorNotes.in part: the answer is a part of the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of thespian, through is, into the start of terrible

annotation.surface: A critic's verdict: the actor was partly awful.
annotation.walkthrough: One performer, the thespian, hides another: thes(PIAN IS T)errible.
annotation.definitionFit: A pianist is a musician who performs on the piano.

entries.clue: Odd fish to study south of dam (6)

indicatorNotes.south of: in a down clue, below, so after

blocks.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
to do a subject is to study it

annotation.surface: A strange fish is being studied downstream of a dam.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fish" looks like wildlife, fitting "dam"; an odd fish is an eccentric person.
annotation.definitionFit: An odd fish is a peculiar person, which is what a weirdo is.

entries.clue: Folds towel, heats log, spreads out (4,2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.spreads out: the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A list of household chores: folding a towel, warming a log, laying things out.
annotation.walkthrough: "Folds" looks like the first chore on the list; it is the definition, a business folding.
annotation.definitionFit: A firm that goes to the wall is ruined; to fold is to close down.

entries.clue: Tramp left in school (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the letter goes inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
l = left

annotation.surface: A vagrant has been left at a school.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tramp" wants to be a noun, a vagrant; it is the verb, to walk heavily.
annotation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily and wearily, which is to plod.

entries.clue: Large working farm’s future (4-5)

blocks.note: l = large, as on clothing labels
a machine that is on is working
a grange is a farm with its buildings

annotation.surface: The prospects for a big farm that is still in business.
annotation.walkthrough: "Future" reads as a noun, prospects; it is an adjective, as in long-range planning.
annotation.definitionFit: A long-range forecast looks far into the future, so the two can stand for each other as adjectives.

entries.clue: Scarce good deed? (5)

blocks.note: thin on the ground, scarce
g = good

annotation.surface: Doing something kind is a rare event.
annotation.walkthrough: "Good deed" reads as one phrase; "good" is only G. The question mark admits a thing is a deed only loosely, as in "do your thing".
annotation.definitionFit: A loose sense the question mark owns up to: an act can be called a thing, as in "a kind thing to do".

entries.clue: Rats eating dead fish (8)

indicatorNotes.eating: the first word swallows the second

blocks.note: "rats!" and "drat!" are both mild curses
gone = dead

annotation.surface: Rodents feeding on a fish carcass.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rats" wants to be rodents; it is the exclamation of annoyance.
annotation.definitionFit: The dragonet is a small, often brightly coloured sea fish.

entries.clue: Victim put back in railway vehicle (6)

indicatorNotes.put back: to put something back is to send it the way it came, so the two pieces are read from end to start

blocks.note: Ry = railway, as in timetables and maps
a tram is a vehicle on rails

annotation.surface: Someone harmed has been put back on a train.
annotation.walkthrough: "Railway vehicle" reads as one thing, a train; it is two pieces, RY and TRAM, which read backwards give the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone who suffers or dies for a cause, a victim.
